findings.title: getForLogin cache ignores organization invalidation and goes stale on org disable/remove
findings.body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin only the per-mode login key is checked for invalidation. In contrast getByOrganization checks both its own key and the organization id, so organization updates evict org queries. Nothing in the change invalidates the login keys when only organization state changes (disable/enable, remove) and getForLogin never consults organization invalidation. A cached login entry therefore keeps internal ids of brokers from an organization that was later disabled or deleted, resolving them via getById still succeeds, so getForLogin keeps returning brokers that no longer qualify for login. The added isEnabled re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only fixes the login page, other callers of getForLogin still get stale results and users can be offered brokers from disabled organizations.

findings.title: Cleanup uses literal "alias" so created test IDPs are never removed
findings.body: In OrganizationCacheTest the cleanup hook uses the literal string "alias" instead of the loop variable, for example get("alias")::remove while the created broker is "org-idp-"+i or "idp-alias-"+i. Removing alias "alias" finds nothing, so the 10 org-idp brokers and the 20+1 idp-alias brokers are never deleted. Leftovers remain in the test realm and are counted by later assertions that expect exact sizes like 5, 10 or 11, making the tests order-dependent and flaky and leaking state to other organization tests. The same literal appears at three places in the new test.
